cands.name: John McBride

money.note: Individuals gave $35,604; PAC money $19,882; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 9th Congressional District. Strength and conditioning coach for more than 40 years. He was the first strength coach at University of the Pacific for 12 years and at St. Mary's High School in Stockton for 13 years. He has not held public office.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California, and the Contra Costa County and San Joaquin County Republican parties, endorsed him for 2026, along with the San Joaquin County California Republican Assembly, San Joaquin Young Republicans and Reform California. Ballotpedia also lists several informal voter-guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no record of any public office held, so there are no legislative actions to report. We could not confirm where he was raised. We found no stated position on data centers, new development or land protection, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas, gun laws, school choice or teacher pay. His campaign pledges on spending and taxes are about federal policy, and he gave no detail on property taxes. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties.

qual.background: Career strength and conditioning coach (University of the Pacific, 12 years; St. Mary's High School, Stockton, 13 years), with a 1984 bachelor's degree from Central Connecticut State University. cands.bio: U.S. representative for California's 9th District since 2023, and for the 10th District from 2019 to 2023. He serves on the Appropriations Committee. Earlier he was a vice president at Bessemer Venture Partners, a Boston Consulting Group consultant and a Modesto Junior College instructor. He holds Stanford, Harvard MBA and MPP degrees.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters and Equality California endorsed him for 2026, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Harder's stance or actions on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, or limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land. We found no documented controversies in the pages reviewed. His campaign site says the state's largest law enforcement organization endorsed him but does not name it, so we left it out. He did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, so his stated positions come from older campaign website text (2018 and 2020) and the current campaign site. Ballotpedia's page was cut off partway through its key-votes list. Birthplace and upbringing are documented, but the page does not give a single move-to-California date because he was born and raised in the state.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

clean-money.evidence: He co-introduced the Ban Corporate PACs Act in November 2019, which would prohibit for-profit corporations from sponsoring, operating or funding political action committees.

second-amendment.evidence: His 2018 campaign website said that California's 10-day waiting periods, assault weapons restrictions and background checks have worked and should be taken nationwide, while also saying he supports responsible gun owners' Second Amendment rights.

pro-life.evidence: His 2018 campaign website said he would advocate for a woman's right to choose and defend Planned Parenthood against attacks on its reimbursement.

back-police-order.evidence: He introduced a bill in 2023 to create a grant program that would let smaller police departments recruit and retain more officers.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: He introduced the Stop the Delta Tunnels Act in February 2023, which would bar the Army Secretary from issuing a permit for the Delta Conveyance Project.

workers-first.evidence: He was one of 46 House Democrats who joined all Republicans in voting for the Laken Riley Act in 2025.
